finding.claim: Tokens with a missing or unknown kid force a live, uncached JWKS HTTP fetch on every request (up to a 30s timeout), before any signature check. This is unauthenticated outbound-request amplification and thread exhaustion. It is not an authentication bypass.
finding.source: The 'kid' field of an unverified JWT header, read in get_signing_key_from_jwt (jwks_client.py:224-226) before signature verification.

trace.note: Header decoded with verify_signature=False; kid taken from unverified header
header.get('kid') passed to get_signing_key; None when absent
match_kid returns None for missing/unknown kid
Successful response overwrites cache; no negative caching anywhere

finding.guards_checked: Scheme restricted to http/https at construction (jwks_client.py:77-82) so no file:// or other scheme SSRF. kid validated as string (api_jws.py:430-432, invoked from decode_complete via _validate_headers at api_jws.py:251). kid used only in equality compare (match_kid, jwks_client.py:242), never in path, URL, or query. No rate limit or negative cache in library. Severity judged low: refetch is the documented key-rotation design and the cost is server-side; mitigation belongs in the application (rate-limit unauthenticated token traffic, negative-cache unknown kids). Not executed; verified by reading only.
